title: Open the hand for the jewel mercy gives
summary: The Jewel of Naam is not seized by force; it is given by mercy and held in the Guru-facing life. Practice receiving before the self-willed grip loses what it wanted to control.
takeaway: Open the hand for the Naam mercy gives.
lifeApplication: When you want instant assurance, pause the demand to feel in charge. Say the Name once with an open hand, and let receiving matter more than proving you possess it.

source.shortMeaning: The Jewel of Naam is received through mercy; the Guru-facing life obtains what the self-willed grip loses.
source.lifeApplication: Unclench the demand to own the moment, and receive the Name as mercy rather than achievement.

evidence.coreClaim: Naam comes as the Lord's merciful gift, not as the ego's possession; the decisive turn is from grasping to Guru-facing reception.
evidence.turn: Let the hand open where mercy is giving the jewel the self cannot manufacture.
evidence.practicalImplication: When you want instant assurance, pause the demand to feel in charge. Say the Name once with an open hand, and let receiving matter more than proving you possess it.
